items.title: Why Bees Matter
items.text: Bees do more than make honey. When a bee visits a flower to drink nectar, pollen sticks to its legs. The bee then carries the pollen to the next flower, and this helps plants make fruit and seeds. Many of the foods we eat, such as apples, almonds, and blueberries, depend on this work. Without bees, farms would produce much less food. That is why many towns now plant wildflowers and protect bee homes. Even a small garden can help.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the passage?
o: Bees make honey from nectar and store it in homes that towns try to protect.
Bees help plants make fruit and seeds, so protecting them keeps food safe.
Gardens are the only places where bees can find enough flowers to live well.
Many kinds of insects are useful to people in cities, farms, and wild places.
qs.why: 중심 내용은 벌이 꽃가루를 옮겨 식물이 열매를 맺게 돕고, 그래서 벌을 보호해야 한다는 것이에요. 나머지는 세부 내용이거나 글에 없거나 너무 넓은 내용이에요.

qs.q: How does pollen move from one flower to another?
o: Strong wind carries it across fields.
Farmers move it with small tools.
Rain washes it from flower to flower.
It sticks to a bee's legs.
qs.why: 본문에 꿀벌이 꽃에서 꿀을 마시는 동안 꽃가루가 다리에 붙는다고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention apples, almonds, and blueberries?
o: To give examples of foods that need bees
To explain which fruits taste the sweetest
To show that farms grow only a few foods
To tell readers what bees like to eat
qs.why: 세 가지는 벌의 일에 의존하는 음식의 예로 쓰였어요.

qs.q: What would most likely happen without bees?
o: Flowers would stop growing in towns and gardens.
Honey would become cheaper in every store.
Farms would grow less food.
Wildflowers would take over all the farms.
qs.why: 글에서 벌이 없으면 농장이 훨씬 적은 음식을 생산할 것이라고 해요.

items.title: Join the Green Club
items.text: Are you tired of seeing trash on the school grounds? The Green Club is looking for new members. Every Wednesday after lunch, we pick up litter, sort the recycling bins, and water the flowers near the gym. Last month we also made posters that remind students to turn off the lights. You do not need any special skills. All you need is a bit of free time and a kind heart. Come to Room 204 this week and bring a friend!

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the notice?
o: The Green Club meets in Room 204 and sometimes makes posters about lights.
Every student must clean the school grounds once a week after lunch.
Students who love the environment should start clubs in many schools.
The Green Club invites students to join and care for the school.
qs.why: 공지의 목적은 학교를 함께 가꿀 새 회원을 모집하는 것이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the notice?
o: To ask students to become members
To report how much trash was collected
To explain how to recycle at home
To thank students for cleaning the gym
qs.why: 필자는 새 회원을 구하고 있어요.

qs.q: According to the notice, what do new members need?
o: Experience in making posters
A friend who is already a member
Some free time and a kind heart
Special tools for sorting trash
qs.why: 특별한 기술은 필요 없고 시간과 친절한 마음이면 된다고 해요.

qs.q: The phrase "tired of" in the first sentence is closest in meaning to
o: proud of
unhappy about
curious about
afraid of
qs.why: be tired of는 '~에 싫증 나다, 지겹다'라는 뜻이라 unhappy about과 가까워요.

items.title: Sleep and Your Brain
items.text: Many teenagers stay up late to study or look at their phones, but sleep is just as important as homework. During sleep, the brain sorts what you learned during the day and stores the important parts. Teenagers need about eight to ten hours each night. Students who sleep too little often find it hard to focus, and they may feel upset more easily. A simple habit, such as putting the phone away thirty minutes before bed, can make falling asleep easier.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why enough sleep matters for teenagers
How to finish homework faster at night
Why phones are bad for the brain
Which foods help students focus in class
qs.why: 글 전체가 충분한 수면이 십대에게 왜 중요한지를 설명해요. 휴대폰은 한 가지 습관으로만 나와요.

qs.q: Which summary adds information that is NOT in the passage?
o: Sleep helps the brain keep what students learned.
Too little sleep can make teenagers upset and unable to focus.
Teenagers who sleep more than ten hours get better grades.
Putting the phone away early can help teenagers fall asleep.
qs.why: 성적에 관한 내용은 글에 없어요. 나머지는 모두 글에 있는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What does the brain do during sleep?
o: It stops working until morning.
It sorts what was learned.
It forgets the hard homework.
It grows bigger every night.
qs.why: 자는 동안 뇌는 낮에 배운 것을 정리하고 중요한 부분을 저장해요.

qs.q: Which advice does the writer give?
o: Study until you feel sleepy.
Sleep during the school day.
Do homework before dinner.
Put your phone away.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 잠들기 30분 전에 휴대폰을 치우라고 조언해요.

items.title: An Email About the Bike
items.text: Hi Mr. Park, I bought a bike from your shop last Saturday, and I am happy with it, but I have a small problem. The front brake makes a loud noise when I stop, and it feels a little loose. I rode only to school and back, so I do not think I damaged it. Could I bring it in this Friday afternoon? I can also leave it with you for a day if you need more time. Thank you for your help. Best, Jiho

qs.q: Which sentence summarizes the email best?
o: Jiho tells Mr. Park that he rides his bike to school and back every day.
Jiho is angry because the shop sold him a broken bike last Saturday.
Jiho asks the shop to look at a noisy brake on his new bike.
Jiho wants to buy a better bike from the shop on Friday afternoon.
qs.why: 이메일의 핵심은 새 자전거의 브레이크 문제를 봐 달라는 부탁이에요.

qs.q: Why does Jiho write that he rode only to school and back?
o: To ask for a cheaper price
To show he did not damage it
To say that school is far away
To explain why he is late
qs.why: 자신이 자전거를 망가뜨리지 않았다는 점을 알리려는 거예요.

qs.q: What is Jiho's feeling about the bike?
o: Bored and tired of it
Proud and completely sure
Angry and ready to quit
Happy but a bit worried
qs.why: 자전거에는 만족하지만 브레이크가 걱정이에요.

qs.q: When does Jiho want to bring the bike?
o: On Friday afternoon
Last Saturday morning
This Sunday evening
On Monday after school
qs.why: Friday afternoon에 가져가도 되는지 묻고 있어요.

items.title: Night Market Notes
items.text: Last weekend my cousin took me to a night market in her city. The air smelled of fried noodles and sweet cakes, and the streets were full of lights. We tried spicy rice cakes first, then shared a cup of fruit juice. My favorite part was a game where you throw rings over bottles. I did not win, but the owner gave me a small sticker anyway. We walked for three hours, and my feet hurt, but I want to go back next year.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the blog post?
o: The writer's feet hurt, so the writer will never visit a night market again.
The writer enjoyed a fun evening of food and games at a night market.
Night markets in big cities sell only fried noodles and sweet cakes.
The writer won a prize by throwing rings over bottles at the market.
qs.why: 중심 내용은 야시장에서 음식과 게임을 즐긴 즐거운 저녁이에요.

qs.q: What did the writer receive from the game owner?
o: A cup of juice
A bag of cakes
A ring
A sticker
qs.why: 이기지는 못했지만 주인이 작은 스티커를 줬어요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel about the visit?
o: Happy, though the walk was tiring
Sorry that the games were too hard
Worried about the crowded streets
Disappointed with the food
qs.why: 발은 아팠지만 내년에 또 가고 싶다고 해요.

qs.q: Which happened first?
o: They shared a cup of fruit juice.
They played the ring-throwing game.
They ate spicy rice cakes.
They walked for three hours.
qs.why: 먼저 매운 떡볶이를 먹고 그다음 주스를 나눠 마셨어요.

items.title: Learning to Swim
items.text: When I was nine, I was afraid of water. My friends jumped into the pool, but I stayed at the edge with my feet in. One summer my aunt offered to teach me. On the first day, I only blew bubbles. On the second day, I held a board and kicked. It took many weeks before I could swim across the pool without help. I still remember how proud I felt when I touched the far wall. Now I tell younger children that small steps really work.

qs.q: What is the main message of the story?
o: Summer is the best time to learn any sport.
Friends should never leave a scared child alone.
Swimming boards are needed for every beginner.
Small steps can help you overcome a fear.
qs.why: 두려움도 작은 단계를 차근차근 밟으면 이겨낼 수 있다는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: Which sentence is too detailed to be a good summary of the whole story?
o: On the second day, the writer held a board and kicked.
A child who feared water slowly learned to swim.
The writer feels proud of overcoming a childhood fear.
After weeks of practice, the writer finally swam across the pool.
qs.why: 둘째 날 이야기는 하루의 세부 내용일 뿐 전체를 요약하지 못해요.

qs.q: Who taught the writer to swim?
o: The writer's friends
A pool lifeguard
The writer's aunt
The writer's cousin
qs.why: 여름에 이모(고모)가 가르쳐 주겠다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "far wall" refer to?
o: The wall behind the writer's house
The wall at the pool's far end
The wall next to the writer's feet
The wall near the school gate
qs.why: 수영장을 가로질러 맞은편 벽을 짚었다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Why Do Volcanoes Erupt?
items.text: Deep under the ground, rock can become so hot that it melts. This melted rock, called magma, is lighter than the rock around it, so it slowly rises. Gas is also trapped inside the magma. As the magma gets closer to the surface, the pressure grows, like in a shaken bottle of soda. At last the magma breaks through a weak spot in the ground and shoots out as lava, ash, and gas. This is an eruption. Scientists watch the ground and the gas near volcanoes to warn people early.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the passage?
o: Hot magma full of gas rises and bursts out, causing an eruption.
Scientists watch the ground near volcanoes in order to warn people early.
Lava, ash, and gas are three things that people can see near mountains.
Soda bottles and volcanoes work in exactly the same way in every case.
qs.why: 마그마가 올라오고 압력이 쌓여 터지는 과정이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention a shaken bottle of soda?
o: To show how scientists test gas
To explain why lava is hot
To show how pressure grows
To describe how magma tastes
qs.why: 소다병과 비교해 압력이 커지는 모습을 쉽게 설명해요.

qs.q: What do scientists do to warn people?
o: They cool the magma with water.
They watch the ground and gas.
They close the weak spots.
They count the rocks nearby.
qs.why: 땅과 가스를 관찰해서 미리 경고해요.

qs.q: The word "trapped" is closest in meaning to
o: lost
heated
hidden
caught
qs.why: trapped는 '갇힌'이라는 뜻이라 caught와 가까워요.

items.title: Dinner Without Phones
items.text: In the Kim family, there is a new rule: no phones at the dinner table. At first, Sora thought the idea was silly. She had to leave her phone in a basket by the door, and the first few dinners felt quiet and strange. But soon the family began to talk about their day, share jokes, and even play word games. Her little brother said it was the best part of the evening. Now Sora checks her messages after dinner, and she says she does not miss the screen at all.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the passage?
o: Sora's brother thinks that word games are the best part of the evening.
Families around the world should put their phones in baskets by the door.
A no-phone rule at dinner helped one family talk and enjoy time together.
Sora was angry about the rule and wanted her old habits back at once.
qs.why: 중심 내용은 식사 중 휴대폰 금지 규칙이 가족 대화를 늘렸다는 것이에요.

qs.q: How did Sora feel about the rule at first?
o: She felt it was a great idea.
She thought it was silly.
She was afraid of her parents.
She was too sleepy to care.
qs.why: 처음에는 어리석다고 생각했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Sora at the end?
o: She dislikes talking with her brother.
She plans to quit using her phone.
She wants a new phone.
She changed her mind about the rule.
qs.why: 마지막에는 화면이 그립지 않다고 하니 생각이 바뀐 것을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: When does Sora check her messages now?
o: After dinner
Before dinner
During dinner
Before school
qs.why: 저녁 식사 후에 메시지를 확인해요.

items.title: School Lunch Review
items.text: Our school's new lunch menu has been out for a month, and students have mixed opinions. Many like the colorful salads and the tasty baked chicken. However, the soup is often cold by the time it reaches the table, and some students say the portions are too small for sports club members. The kitchen staff have promised to buy warmer serving trays and to offer extra rice on request. If you have more ideas, you can write them on the board in the hallway.

qs.q: Which sentence summarizes the review best?
o: The new school lunches are so bad that students should bring their own food.
The new lunches have good and bad points, and the staff will make changes.
Students may write their ideas on the board that stands in the hallway.
The kitchen staff have decided to serve baked chicken every day.
qs.why: 장단점이 섞여 있고 급식실이 개선하겠다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: What is one problem mentioned in the review?
o: The salads are not colorful.
The chicken is not baked enough.
The hallway board is broken.
The soup arrives cold.
qs.why: 수프가 식어서 도착한다는 문제가 언급돼요.

qs.q: What will the kitchen staff do?
o: Buy warmer trays and more rice
Remove the salad from the menu
Make the soup much sweeter
Ask club members to cook
qs.why: 더 따뜻한 쟁반을 사고 요청 시 밥을 더 줄 거예요.

qs.q: The word "mixed" in the first sentence means
o: completely happy
very confused
good and bad
easy to change
qs.why: mixed opinions는 좋은 의견과 나쁜 의견이 섞여 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: How a Rainbow Forms
items.text: A rainbow needs two things: sunlight and water drops. When the sun shines after or during rain, light enters the tiny drops in the air. Inside each drop, the white light bends and splits into many colors, from red to violet. The colors then bounce back toward your eyes. To see a rainbow, you must stand with the sun behind you and look at the rain in front of you. That is why you can see one in the morning or late afternoon, but almost never at noon in summer.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the passage?
o: Rainbows are seen in the morning or late afternoon more than at noon in summer.
Red and violet are the two colors found at the ends of every rainbow shape.
Rain falls whenever the sun is shining brightly behind a person's back.
Rainbows appear when sunlight bends and splits inside water drops in the air.
qs.why: 중심 내용은 햇빛이 물방울 속에서 꺾이고 나뉘어 무지개가 생긴다는 것이에요.

qs.q: Where should you stand to see a rainbow?
o: With the sun behind you
With the sun in front of you
Directly under the rain
Far from any water
qs.why: 해가 등 뒤에 있어야 맞은편 비를 볼 수 있어요.

qs.q: When can you usually see a rainbow in summer?
o: At noon on a clear day
Late at night after the rain
In the morning or late afternoon
Only when the sun is behind the rain
qs.why: 본문: 아침이나 늦은 오후에는 볼 수 있지만 여름 정오에는 거의 볼 수 없어요.

qs.q: Which happens first?
o: The colors bounce back to your eyes.
Light enters a water drop.
White light splits into colors.
You look at the rain.
qs.why: 빛이 물방울에 들어간 뒤 색으로 나뉘고 반사돼요.

items.title: New Library Hours
items.text: Starting next Monday, the town library will open one hour earlier on weekdays, at eight o'clock in the morning. It will still close at six in the evening. On Saturdays, the children's room will stay open until five so that families can read together after soccer practice. Please note that the computer room will be closed for repairs during the first two weeks of the new schedule. Library cards can be renewed online, which means you no longer have to wait in line at the front desk.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
o: To announce the library's new hours
To invite people to a soccer game
To ask readers to return their books
To sell new library cards
qs.why: 새로운 운영 시간과 변경 사항을 알리는 공지예요.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary?
o: The library will close at six in the evening on all weekdays.
The library has been closed for a long time because of repairs.
The library is changing its hours and adding some services.
The library will give free cards to all children who play soccer.
qs.why: 운영 시간 변경과 몇 가지 새 서비스가 중심이에요.

qs.q: Which service is closed for the first two weeks?
o: The children's room
The computer room
The front desk
The online card system
qs.why: 컴퓨터실은 처음 2주 동안 수리로 닫혀요.

qs.q: What is the benefit of renewing a card online?
o: People can borrow more books each time.
People can use the computers at night.
People can read in the children's room.
People can skip the line at the desk.
qs.why: 온라인으로 갱신하면 데스크에서 줄을 설 필요가 없어요.

items.title: Kimchi Making Day
items.text: Every November, my grandmother's village holds a kimchi making day. Neighbors gather in her yard with huge bowls of salted cabbage and red pepper paste. The adults mix the paste while the children carry the cabbages. The work is hard, but the yard is filled with laughter and stories. At the end of the day, each family takes home several boxes of kimchi and shares a warm meal with the others. My grandmother says that making kimchi together is a way to keep the village close.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The best way to mix red pepper paste
A child's first job on the farm
A village's shared kimchi tradition
Why cabbage is salted before winter
qs.why: 마을 사람들이 함께 김장하며 가까워지는 전통이 중심이에요.

qs.q: Which sentence is too narrow to be a summary of the passage?
o: Neighbors make kimchi together every November in a village.
Children carry the cabbages and adults mix the paste.
Making kimchi is a shared task that also builds friendships.
Families make kimchi together and enjoy a meal at the end.
qs.why: 아이들과 어른들의 역할 이야기는 세부 내용이라 전체 요약으로는 좁아요.

qs.q: What does the grandmother believe?
o: Kimchi tastes best when made alone.
Children should not help with the work.
November is the coldest month.
Working together keeps people close.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 함께 김치를 담그는 것이 마을을 가깝게 한다고 해요.

qs.q: What does each family get at the end of the day?
o: Several boxes of kimchi
A bowl of red pepper paste
A bag of salted cabbage
A new cooking pot
qs.why: 각 가족이 김치 몇 통을 집에 가져가요.

items.title: Life in the Desert
items.text: A desert looks empty, but many animals have found clever ways to live there. The fennec fox has huge ears that give off heat, so its body stays cool. Camels can drink a great deal of water at once and then travel for days without drinking. Many small animals sleep in cool holes during the hot day and come out only at night to look for food. These habits do not make life easy, but they help the animals survive where water is rare.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the passage?
o: Fennec foxes have big ears, and camels can walk for days without any water.
Desert animals have special ways to survive with little water.
Deserts are the hottest places on Earth, and no plants can grow there.
Small animals leave their holes only at night because they are afraid of camels.
qs.why: 중심 내용은 사막 동물들이 물이 적은 곳에서 살아남는 방법이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, why do fennec foxes have large ears?
o: To hear sounds from far away
To dig holes in hot sand
To store water for later
To let body heat escape
qs.why: 큰 귀가 열을 내보내 몸을 시원하게 해 줘요.

qs.q: When do many small desert animals look for food?
o: At night
At noon
In the early afternoon
Just after the rain
qs.why: 더운 낮에는 구멍에서 자고 밤에 나와요.

qs.q: The word "rare" is closest in meaning to
o: easy to carry
good to drink
hard to find
far from home
qs.why: rare는 '드문'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Staying Safe Online
items.text: The internet is a wonderful place to learn and play, but it also has risks. First, never share your password with anyone except your parents. Second, think before you post a photo, because once it is online, it can be copied by others. Third, if a stranger sends you a message that makes you feel uncomfortable, do not answer; tell an adult at once. Finally, remember that not everything you read online is true. Checking more than one website can help you find the facts.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the passage?
o: Passwords are the most important thing to protect, and parents can always see them.
Photos should never be posted online because other people always copy them.
The internet is a dangerous place where children must stay away from strangers.
Internet users should follow simple rules to stay safe and find the truth.
qs.why: 여러 가지 안전 수칙을 모아 온라인에서 자신을 보호하라는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, who may know your password?
o: Your parents
Your best friends
Your teachers
Anyone who asks nicely
qs.why: 비밀번호는 부모님 외에는 공유하지 말라고 해요.

qs.q: What should you do if a stranger's message makes you uncomfortable?
o: Reply and ask who the person is.
Block your parents' account.
Tell an adult right away.
Delete your photos online.
qs.why: 대답하지 말고 즉시 어른에게 알리라고 해요.

qs.q: Why does the writer suggest checking more than one website?
o: Many websites are too slow.
Some information online may not be true.
Parents like to read many pages.
Different sites have different passwords.
qs.why: 온라인의 모든 내용이 사실은 아니기 때문이에요.

items.title: The Lost Dog
items.text: On Tuesday afternoon, Min-ho saw a small brown dog sitting alone near the bus stop. It had no collar, and it was shaking in the cold. Min-ho gave it half of his sandwich and called his mother. Together they took the dog to the animal clinic, where a doctor checked it and found a tiny tag under its fur. The tag had a phone number. That evening, a girl came to the clinic with tears in her eyes and hugged her dog tightly. Min-ho smiled all the way home.

qs.q: What is the best summary of the story?
o: Min-ho helped a lost dog get back to its owner.
Min-ho found a sandwich while he was waiting at a bus stop.
A doctor at an animal clinic took care of many dogs in the cold.
A girl was crying because she could not find the way home.
qs.why: 민호가 길 잃은 개를 주인에게 돌려보내 준 이야기예요.

qs.q: How did the clinic find the owner?
o: The dog barked at the girl.
Min-ho looked at the collar.
A phone number was on a tag.
A neighbor knew the dog.
qs.why: 수의사가 털 속에서 전화번호가 적힌 작은 태그를 발견했어요.

qs.q: How did the girl feel when she saw her dog?
o: Surprised and angry
Relieved and happy
Bored and sleepy
Shy and nervous
qs.why: 눈물을 글썽이며 강아지를 꼭 안았으니 안도하고 기뻤어요.

qs.q: Why did Min-ho smile all the way home?
o: He was going to keep the dog.
He had won a school prize.
He was glad to be warm again.
He felt good about helping.
qs.why: 도움을 줬다는 뿌듯함 때문이라고 추론할 수 있어요.

items.title: Spring Festival Announcement
items.text: Our school will hold its Spring Festival on the first Friday of May. Classes will end after lunch, and the festival will begin at one o'clock on the main playground. Each class will run a booth, such as a food stand, a game corner, or a small art show. The music club will play on the stage at three. Parents and neighbors are welcome, and the money from the booths will be used to buy new books for the library. Please send your ideas for booths to your homeroom teacher by next Wednesday.

qs.q: Which sentence summarizes the announcement best?
o: The music club will perform on the school stage at three o'clock.
Every class must run a food stand on the first Friday of May.
The school will hold a spring festival to raise money for books.
Parents and neighbors must pay to enter the school playground.
qs.why: 봄 축제 안내이고 수익금이 도서관 책 구입에 쓰인다는 점이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: What will the money from the booths be used for?
o: Paying the music club
Buying new books
Fixing the playground
Making school posters
qs.why: 부스 수익금은 도서관의 새 책을 사는 데 쓰여요.

qs.q: What should students do by next Wednesday?
o: Bring snacks and drinks to the festival
Practice with the music club
Invite their neighbors
Tell their teacher their booth ideas
qs.why: 다음 주 수요일까지 담임 선생님께 부스 아이디어를 보내야 해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the announcement?
o: To give details and ask for ideas
To change the rules for classes
To close the school early
To praise the music club
qs.why: 축제 정보를 알리고 아이디어를 요청해요.

items.title: Why Drink Water?
items.text: Your body is about sixty percent water. Water carries food energy to your cells, keeps your temperature steady, and helps your body get rid of waste. When you do not drink enough, you may feel tired or get a headache. Many people wait until they feel thirsty, but thirst is a late signal. A better habit is to take small sips throughout the day. If plain water seems boring, you can add a slice of lemon or cucumber for flavor.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to make lemon and cucumber drinks
Why and how to drink water regularly
Why tired people should sleep more
Which sports drinks give the most energy
qs.why: 물이 몸에 하는 일과 규칙적으로 마시는 방법이 중심이에요.

qs.q: Which sentence should be left out of a short summary?
o: Water does important jobs inside the body.
Not drinking enough water can make you tired.
It is better to sip water through the whole day.
You can add lemon or cucumber for flavor.
qs.why: 레몬이나 오이를 넣는 것은 부수적인 세부 정보예요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what is thirst?
o: A late signal from the body
A sure sign of good health
A habit that can be learned
A way to cool the cells
qs.why: 목마름은 늦게 오는 신호라고 해요.

qs.q: What can happen when you drink too little water?
o: Your body will grow warmer.
Your food will taste better.
You may get a headache.
You will sleep for many hours.
qs.why: 수분이 부족하면 피곤하거나 두통이 생길 수 있어요.

items.title: A Day at the Animal Shelter
items.text: Last Saturday, I volunteered at an animal shelter for the first time. My job was to clean the cages, fill the water bowls, and walk the dogs. At first I felt nervous because some dogs were big and loud. A worker named Ms. Han showed me how to speak softly and give each dog time to sniff my hand. By the afternoon, a shy gray puppy was following me everywhere. When I said goodbye, I promised to return. Helping animals was tiring, but it made me feel useful.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the passage?
o: A shy gray puppy followed a worker named Ms. Han all afternoon.
Animal shelters need volunteers because big dogs are loud and scary.
The writer decided never to go back because the work was too tiring.
A new volunteer felt nervous but enjoyed helping shelter animals.
qs.why: 처음 봉사한 사람이 긴장했지만 보람을 느꼈다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: How did the writer feel at first?
o: Nervous
Bored
Proud
Angry
qs.why: 처음에는 큰 개들 때문에 긴장했어요.

qs.q: What did Ms. Han teach the writer?
o: To train puppies to sit
To wash big dogs quickly
To be gentle with dogs
To open the cages safely
qs.why: 부드럽게 말하고 개가 손 냄새를 맡게 하는 법을 알려 줬어요.

qs.q: What does the ending suggest about the writer?
o: The writer wants to adopt every dog.
The writer wants to volunteer again.
The writer dislikes the shelter workers.
The writer plans to stop helping animals.
qs.why: 다시 오겠다고 약속했으니 또 봉사하고 싶어 해요.

items.title: The Slow Train
items.text: My father likes trains more than planes. He says a train ride is a trip in itself, not just a way to arrive. Last winter we took a slow train across the mountains to visit my uncle. Through the window we saw frozen lakes, small villages, and farmers walking with their cows. We played cards, ate rice balls, and talked more than we do at home. The trip took eight hours, which is much longer than a plane, but I did not feel bored for one minute.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Enjoying a long train journey
The reasons why planes are dangerous
How to visit an uncle in the mountains
What farmers do in the winter
qs.why: 기차 여행 자체를 즐긴다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: Which sentence is too broad to be a good summary?
o: A slow train ride was a fun trip for the writer's family.
The writer enjoyed seeing the views and talking during a train trip.
Traveling is a good way to spend time with family.
A long trip by train felt interesting rather than boring.
qs.why: 여행 일반에 관한 문장은 이 글만의 내용을 담지 못해 너무 넓어요.

qs.q: How long did the trip take?
o: Eighteen hours
Eight hours
Two days
Three hours
qs.why: 여행은 8시간 걸렸다고 해요.

qs.q: What does the father mean by "a trip in itself"?
o: The train is cheaper than other ways.
Trains always arrive on time.
Only long trips are worth taking.
The ride is part of the fun.
qs.why: 도착뿐 아니라 이동 자체가 여행의 일부라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Giving Bottles a Second Life
items.text: Every year, people throw away millions of plastic bottles. Instead of tossing them in the trash, you can find new uses for them. A bottle with the top cut off can become a pen holder or a small pot for seeds. Two bottles taped together make a bird feeder if you cut a few holes for the seeds. Some schools even use hundreds of bottles to build a greenhouse wall. These ideas save money, cut down on trash, and show that old things can still be useful.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the passage?
o: A pen holder is the simplest thing that can be made from a plastic bottle.
Schools build greenhouses because they cannot buy glass for the walls.
Used bottles can be turned into useful things, which reduces trash.
People throw away too many bottles, and the government should stop them.
qs.why: 버려지는 병을 다시 쓰는 아이디어로 쓰레기를 줄인다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: What can two bottles taped together become?
o: A pen holder
A bird feeder
A greenhouse wall
A seed pot
qs.why: 병 두 개를 붙이고 구멍을 내면 새 모이통이 돼요.

qs.q: What is the writer's purpose?
o: To ask schools for money
To sell plastic products
To explain how bottles are made
To show how to reuse bottles
qs.why: 병을 재사용하는 방법을 제안하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a benefit?
o: It makes the bottles taste better.
It saves money.
It reduces the amount of trash.
It shows old things can be useful.
qs.why: 맛에 관한 이야기는 없어요. 나머지 세 가지는 마지막 문장에 나와요.

items.title: The Moving Sea
items.text: If you spend a day at the beach, you will notice that the water goes up and down twice a day. These changes are called tides. They are caused mainly by the pull of the moon, which tugs gently on the ocean. When the water is high, waves reach far up the sand; when it is low, the beach becomes wide and you can find shells and small crabs. Fishers and sailors check a tide table before they go out, because the depth of the water affects their boats.

qs.q: What is the best summary of the passage?
o: Fishers use tide tables to find small crabs and shells on the sand.
Tides are daily changes in sea level that affect people at the beach.
The moon is a large ball of rock that pulls on every beach in the world.
Waves always reach far up the sand when people want to swim.
qs.why: 조수가 하루에 두 번 바닷물 높이가 바뀌는 현상이고 사람들에게 영향을 준다는 것이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what mainly causes tides?
o: The strength of the wind
The heat of the sun
The shape of the beach
The pull of the moon
qs.why: 달의 인력이 주된 원인이에요.

qs.q: Why do sailors check a tide table?
o: Water depth affects their boats.
They want to find shells and crabs.
They need to know the weather.
They want to avoid the moon.
qs.why: 물의 깊이가 배에 영향을 주기 때문이에요.

qs.q: When can you find shells and small crabs?
o: When the tide is high
When the waves are very big
When the tide is low
When the moon is bright
qs.why: 물이 빠지면 해변이 넓어져 조개와 작은 게를 찾을 수 있어요.

items.title: My First Guitar Lessons
items.text: Learning the guitar is harder than I expected. In my first week, my fingers hurt from pressing the strings, and every chord sounded like a cat in trouble. I almost quit. Then my teacher told me to practice for just ten minutes a day instead of one long hour once a week. I tried it, and after a month I could play three chords. Last night I played a simple song for my family, and my mother clapped so loudly that the neighbors may have heard her.

qs.q: Which sentence summarizes the passage best?
o: The writer's mother loves loud music and often claps for her neighbors.
The writer stopped the lessons because sore fingers made playing painful.
Guitar is the most difficult instrument that any student can learn.
The writer improved at the guitar by practicing a little every day.
qs.why: 매일 조금씩 연습해 실력이 늘었다는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: What did the teacher advise?
o: Practice ten minutes every day.
Practice one hour on the weekend.
Change to an easier instrument.
Play only for the family.
qs.why: 하루 10분씩 연습하라고 조언했어요.

qs.q: What does "like a cat in trouble" suggest about the sound?
o: It sounded sleepy.
It sounded very quiet.
It sounded bad.
It sounded beautiful.
qs.why: 고양이가 곤경에 빠졌을 때의 소리 같다는 건 듣기 안 좋았다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel at the end?
o: Tired and bored
Proud and happy
Angry and worried
Shy and sad
qs.why: 가족 앞에서 연주하고 박수를 받아 뿌듯하고 기뻐요.

items.title: Gardens in the Sky
items.text: In crowded cities, there is little room for parks, so some people are turning rooftops into gardens. On top of tall buildings, they grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers in boxes of soil. These green roofs have many benefits. Plants keep the building cooler in summer, so less air conditioning is needed. Rain soaks into the soil instead of rushing into the streets. Rooftop gardens also give workers a quiet place to rest. Some even have beehives, which provide honey for the neighborhood.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How rooftop gardens help cities and people
Why tall buildings are good for bees
Which vegetables grow best in boxes
How workers can relax at lunchtime
qs.why: 옥상 정원의 여러 이점이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: Which is the best summary?
o: Rooftop gardens are a place where bees make honey for the whole city.
Cities should build parks on the ground and not on top of buildings.
Rooftop gardens cool buildings, hold rain, and give people rest.
Workers use boxes of soil to grow herbs for their lunch.
qs.why: 여러 이점을 아우르는 문장이 좋은 요약이에요.

qs.q: How do green roofs help in summer?
o: They make rain heavier.
They cool the buildings.
They catch more sunlight.
They stop all the noise.
qs.why: 식물이 건물을 시원하게 해 에어컨 사용이 줄어요.

qs.q: What happens to rain on a green roof?
o: It flows to the bees.
It stays in the boxes forever.
It rushes into the streets.
It soaks into the soil.
qs.why: 빗물이 흙에 스며들어 거리로 쏟아지지 않아요.

items.title: Better Homework Habits
items.text: Many students feel stressed by homework, but a few habits can make it easier. First, choose a quiet place and put away anything that might distract you. Second, make a list of tasks and begin with the hardest one while your mind is fresh. Third, take a short break every forty minutes to stretch or drink water. Finally, check your work before you pack your bag. Students who follow these steps often finish earlier and have more free time in the evening.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the passage?
o: Students should always begin with the hardest task and then go to bed.
Teachers give too much homework, so students feel stressed all evening.
Simple study habits can help students finish homework with less stress.
A quiet room is the only thing a student needs for good homework.
qs.why: 간단한 공부 습관이 숙제 스트레스를 줄여 준다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, when should students start the hardest task?
o: Near the end of the evening
At the start, while you are fresh
After a long break in the evening
Right before checking the work
qs.why: 머리가 맑을 때 가장 어려운 것부터 시작하라고 해요.

qs.q: How often does the writer suggest taking a short break?
o: Every twenty minutes
Once a day
After each task
Every forty minutes
qs.why: 40분마다 짧게 쉬라고 해요.

qs.q: What is the likely result of these habits?
o: Students finish sooner and have free time.
Students need less sleep.
Teachers give them more homework to do.
Students forget the hard parts.
qs.why: 일찍 끝내고 저녁 시간이 늘어난다고 해요.

items.title: Learning from a Loss
items.text: Our school soccer team lost 6 to 0 last Thursday. Everyone was quiet on the bus ride home, and a few players were close to tears. Then our coach said something I will not forget. She told us that the score showed only one day, not who we were. She asked each of us to name one thing we had done well. Hana said she had stopped two goals, and Joon said he had never given up running. By the time we arrived, we were already planning the next practice.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: A goalkeeper stopped two goals and became the star player.
A kind coach helped the team look past a bad loss.
The team plans to change the coach after the heavy loss.
Soccer is a game in which the score is not important at all.
qs.why: 코치의 말이 팀이 패배를 딛고 다시 힘을 내게 했다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: How did the team feel on the bus at first?
o: Excited and loud
Angry at the referee
Sleepy and relaxed
Sad and quiet
qs.why: 버스 안은 조용했고 눈물을 글썽이는 선수도 있었어요.

qs.q: What did the coach want each player to do?
o: Name one good thing they did
Promise to win the next game
Blame the other team
Write a letter to the school
qs.why: 각자 잘한 점 한 가지를 말하게 했어요.

qs.q: What does the ending show about the team?
o: They gave up the sport.
They were angry at one another.
They felt hopeful again.
They forgot the game.
qs.why: 도착할 때쯤엔 다음 연습을 계획하고 있었으니 다시 희망을 찾았어요.

items.title: Why Do We Yawn?
items.text: Everyone yawns, even babies before they are born. People often think that we yawn only when we are sleepy, but scientists say that is not the whole story. One idea is that a big yawn pulls in cool air and helps cool the brain. Another idea is that yawning wakes us up when we need to stay alert. Yawns also seem to spread from person to person; seeing someone yawn can make you do the same. Scientists are still studying why this happens, so there is no final answer yet.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the passage?
o: People yawn only when they are very tired, and babies yawn the most of all.
Cool air is the main reason why a person's brain begins to work well again.
Yawning is catching, so people should avoid looking at each other's faces at all.
Scientists have different ideas about why people yawn, but no final answer.
qs.why: 하품의 이유에 대한 여러 가설이 있지만 아직 확실한 답은 없다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: Which idea about yawning is mentioned?
o: It may cool the brain.
It makes the heart slow down.
It helps people breathe less.
It warms the body at night.
qs.why: 큰 하품이 시원한 공기를 들여 뇌를 식힌다는 가설이 나와요.

qs.q: What does "spread" mean in this passage?
o: Become wider in size
Make something much thinner
Pass from person to person
Be hidden from other people
qs.why: 하품이 사람에서 사람으로 옮는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by "that is not the whole story" in the second sentence?
o: Scientists wrote a long book about sleep.
Sleepiness is only one reason people yawn.
Babies have a different story about yawning.
The writer will tell a longer story later.
qs.why: 'that is not the whole story'는 졸릴 때만 하품하는 것이 전부는 아니라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Beach Clean-Up Report
items.text: On Sunday morning, forty students and teachers cleaned Dolphin Beach. In two hours, the group filled thirty bags with bottles, plastic bags, and old fishing nets. A student named Yuna counted the items and found that more than half were pieces of plastic. Some volunteers also saw a small crab hiding in a torn cup. When the work was finished, everyone sat on the sand to eat sandwiches and plan another clean-up for next month. The group hopes more families will join them next time.

qs.q: What is the best summary of the report?
o: A group of students and teachers worked together to clean up a beach.
Yuna counted the plastic and discovered a crab in a cup on the beach.
Forty students and teachers ate sandwiches on the sand after school.
Fishing nets and old bottles are very dangerous for people at the beach.
qs.why: 학생들과 선생님들이 함께 해변을 청소한 활동이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: What did most of the collected items turn out to be?
o: Old fishing nets
Glass bottles
Plastic pieces
Pieces of paper
qs.why: 절반 넘게가 플라스틱 조각이었어요.

qs.q: What do the volunteers plan to do next month?
o: Visit the crab
Hold another clean-up
Have a sandwich party
Build a new beach
qs.why: 다음 달에 또 청소하기로 계획해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last sentence?
o: To say the beach is now clean
To thank the teachers for helping
To describe the weather
To show they want more helpers
qs.why: 더 많은 가족이 참여하길 바란다는 희망을 나타내요.

items.title: A Visit to the Science Museum
items.text: Our class visited the science museum on Friday. In the first hall, we touched a model of the solar system and learned that Earth is the third planet from the sun. The second hall had a machine that made a small tornado out of mist, and we watched it spin for a long time. After lunch, we made paper airplanes and tested which one flew the farthest. Mine landed in a plant pot, which made everyone laugh. On the bus, my teacher asked us to write one new fact we had learned.

qs.q: Which sentence summarizes the passage best?
o: The writer's paper airplane flew farther than any of the others.
Earth is the third planet from the sun and the biggest of all.
The class had a fun and educational day at a science museum.
Museums are better places to learn science than classrooms.
qs.why: 과학관에서 즐겁게 배운 하루가 중심이에요.

qs.q: What did the students do in the second hall?
o: They touched a model of the sun.
They watched a mist tornado.
They flew paper airplanes.
They ate their lunch.
qs.why: 두 번째 전시관에는 안개로 만든 작은 토네이도가 있었어요.

qs.q: Why did everyone laugh?
o: The machine suddenly broke down.
The teacher dropped a model.
Someone fell on the bus.
The plane landed in a plant pot.
qs.why: 필자의 종이비행기가 화분에 떨어져 웃음이 났어요.

qs.q: What did the teacher ask for on the bus?
o: A new fact from each student
A short story about the sun
A list of all the planets
A paper airplane
qs.why: 버스에서 새로 배운 사실 하나를 쓰라고 했어요.

items.title: The Tea Ceremony Idea
items.text: In many countries, drinking tea is more than a way to quench thirst. In some places, a tea gathering is slow and quiet, with every movement planned carefully. The host warms the cups, pours the tea, and offers it with both hands. Guests thank the host and drink in small sips. In other places, tea is shared loudly among friends, with sweets and long talks. Different as they are, both styles show the same idea: tea is a way to honor guests and enjoy time together.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the passage?
o: Hosts must use both hands and quiet voices whenever they serve tea.
Tea customs differ, but they all bring people together.
Loud tea gatherings with sweets are better than slow, quiet ones.
Tea is the most popular drink in countries around the whole world.
qs.why: 다른 방식이지만 차는 손님을 존중하고 함께 시간을 보내는 방법이라는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: How is tea served at a quiet gathering?
o: With sweets and loud talk
From a large pot on the floor
By the guests themselves
With both hands
qs.why: 주인이 두 손으로 차를 건네요.

qs.q: What do the two styles have in common?
o: They honor the guests.
They use the same cups.
They have only quiet music.
They cost very little.
qs.why: 마지막 문장: 두 방식 모두 손님을 존중하고 함께 즐기는 방법이에요.

qs.q: The phrase "quench thirst" is closest in meaning to
o: start to feel hungry
keep something warm
stop feeling thirsty
make a drink sweet
qs.why: quench thirst는 갈증을 해소한다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Paper or Screen?
items.text: Many students now read on tablets, but others prefer paper books. Paper readers say that they remember the story better because they can feel how far they have read. They also say the pages do not hurt their eyes. Screen readers answer that a tablet can hold hundreds of books, so they never need to carry a heavy bag. A tablet can also make letters bigger for easier reading. Experts say both ways work well; the best choice depends on what is comfortable for each reader.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to choose a heavy bag for school
Why tablets cost more than books
Which stories are good for students
The pros of paper and screen reading
qs.why: 종이책과 화면 읽기 각각의 장점을 비교하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Which summary best matches the last sentence?
o: Neither way always wins, so readers should pick what suits them.
Paper books are better because they are easy to feel and carry.
Tablets are better, so schools should stop buying paper books.
Experts say that most students do not read enough books.
qs.why: 전문가는 둘 다 좋으며 개인에게 편한 쪽을 고르라고 해요.

qs.q: Why do some readers like tablets?
o: Pages are easier to turn.
Letters cannot be changed.
It can hold many books.
They never need batteries.
qs.why: 태블릿에는 수백 권을 담을 수 있어 가방이 가벼워요.

qs.q: What is true about paper readers?
o: They need bigger letters.
They can feel their progress.
They carry more than one bag.
They read faster than others.
qs.why: 종이책 독자는 어디까지 읽었는지 느낄 수 있다고 해요.

items.title: The New Student
items.text: When Mina walked into our classroom on Monday, nobody knew what to say. She had moved from another city, and she held her bag tightly in front of her. During the morning break, I noticed she was sitting alone. I remembered how lonely I felt when I started at this school, so I walked over and asked her to join our card game. She smiled for the first time. By Wednesday, she was laughing with us at lunch, and she taught us a new game from her old school.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the story?
o: The writer's kind invitation helped a new student feel welcome.
Mina taught her classmates a game from her old school on Wednesday.
The writer felt lonely because no one asked the writer to play cards.
Students from other cities should be careful when they change schools.
qs.why: 필자의 친절한 초대가 전학생이 적응하게 도왔다는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer ask Mina to join the game?
o: The teacher told the writer to ask Mina.
Mina asked the writer for some help.
The writer remembered feeling lonely.
The game needed one more player to start.
qs.why: 자신이 처음 왔을 때 외로웠던 것이 기억났기 때문이에요.

qs.q: How did Mina feel on Monday morning?
o: Excited and proud
Nervous and alone
Angry and bored
Tired and hungry
qs.why: 가방을 꼭 쥐고 혼자 앉아 있었어요.

qs.q: What happened by Wednesday?
o: Mina moved to another city.
Mina stopped playing games.
Mina changed her seat.
Mina laughed with the group.
qs.why: 수요일에는 점심때 함께 웃고 있었어요.

items.title: Earthquake Drill
items.text: Last week, our school held an earthquake drill. When the alarm rang, we dropped under our desks, covered our heads, and held on to the desk legs. After one minute, the teacher led us in a line to the playground, away from windows and tall walls. The principal said that the most important thing is to stay calm and listen to instructions. We all felt a bit silly at first, but later we understood that practicing now could keep us safe if a real earthquake ever happens.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: The principal ran the school alarm for a very long time.
Windows and tall walls are the most dangerous things at school.
Drills teach students how to stay safe in an earthquake.
Students feel silly when they learn something new in class.
qs.why: 대피 훈련이 안전을 배우는 기회라는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: What did students do first when the alarm rang?
o: They ran to the playground.
They got under their desks.
They opened the windows.
They called their parents.
qs.why: 먼저 책상 아래로 몸을 낮췄어요.

qs.q: Why did the students move away from windows and tall walls?
o: The playground was noisy.
The teacher liked the line.
The alarm was too loud.
These places can be unsafe.
qs.why: 창문과 높은 벽 근처는 위험하다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does the writer say about the drill?
o: It seemed silly but was useful.
It was much too long and tiring.
It should be held every day.
It made everyone feel afraid.
qs.why: 처음엔 어색했지만 나중에 연습의 가치를 이해했어요.

items.title: The Story of the Bicycle
items.text: The first bicycles looked very different from the ones we ride today. About two hundred years ago, some had no pedals at all; riders pushed against the ground with their feet to move. Later, inventors added pedals to the front wheel, which made the bike faster but harder to ride. Then, makers put a chain on the back wheel and gave both wheels the same size. This design was safer and easier, and it is still the basic shape of most bicycles. Today, people use bikes for fun, sport, and daily travel.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the passage?
o: People today use bikes for fun, sport, and daily travel.
Bicycles changed over time until they reached today's safe design.
People today use bikes only for sport and for fun on weekends.
Inventors made bikes faster by putting the pedals on large front wheels.
qs.why: 시간이 지나며 자전거가 오늘날의 안전한 모양으로 발전했다는 것이 중심이에요.

qs.q: What made later bicycles easier and safer?
o: Large pedals on the front wheel only
A larger back wheel
No pedals at all
A back-wheel chain and equal wheels
qs.why: 뒷바퀴 체인과 같은 크기의 두 바퀴가 더 안전하고 쉬웠어요.

qs.q: What was a problem with the bikes that had pedals on the front wheel?
o: They were harder to ride.
They were too slow for racing.
They had no seat for the rider.
They could only be used on sand.
qs.why: 앞바퀴에 페달을 단 자전거는 더 빨랐지만 타기 더 어려웠다고 해요.

qs.q: How did riders move the earliest bikes?
o: By using a very small engine
By turning a handle
By pushing off the ground
By pedaling on the back wheel
qs.why: 발로 땅을 밀어 앞으로 나아갔어요.

items.title: Why Breakfast Matters
items.text: Many students skip breakfast because they are in a hurry, but this can be a mistake. After a night of sleep, the body needs fuel. Students who eat breakfast often listen better in class and feel more cheerful. A good breakfast does not have to take long. A bowl of oatmeal with fruit, a boiled egg and toast, or a glass of milk with a banana can be ready in minutes. A sugary snack may give quick energy, but it fades fast and leaves you hungry again before lunch.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to make oatmeal with fruit quickly
Why students never have time in the morning
How sugary snacks are made
Why students should eat breakfast
qs.why: 건강한 아침 식사가 학생에게 왜 좋은지가 중심이에요.

qs.q: Which sentence is too narrow to be the main idea of the passage?
o: A boiled egg and toast is one quick breakfast that a student can make.
Eating breakfast helps students feel and learn better.
Students should not skip breakfast, because it is quick to make and good for them.
Breakfast gives students energy for the day, and a good one is easy to prepare.
qs.why: 삶은 달걀과 토스트는 글에 나온 한 가지 예시일 뿐이라 중심 생각으로는 너무 좁아요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what happens after a sugary snack?
o: You sleep for many hours.
You listen better.
You get hungry soon.
You need less lunch.
qs.why: 당분 간식은 에너지가 금방 사라져 점심 전에 다시 배가 고파요.

qs.q: What does the writer want to say with "this can be a mistake"?
o: Students should eat only fruit.
Skipping breakfast is unwise.
Hurrying is a good habit.
Mornings are always busy.
qs.why: 아침을 거르는 것은 좋지 않다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Moon Shapes
items.text: The moon seems to change shape every night, but it is not really changing. The moon does not make its own light; we see it because it reflects sunlight. As the moon travels around Earth, we see different amounts of its bright side. When the whole bright side faces us, we see a full moon. A week later, we see only half of it. After about two weeks, the moon looks like a thin line or disappears from sight. The whole cycle, from one full moon to the next, takes about a month.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the passage?
o: The moon seems to change shape as we see different parts of its lit side.
The moon is a ball of rock that makes its own light and really changes shape every night.
A full moon appears one week after the moon looks like a thin line.
The moon is closest to Earth when it looks like a thin line.
qs.why: 달 모양이 변해 보이는 이유가 중심이에요. 달은 스스로 빛나지 않아요.

qs.q: Why can we see the moon?
o: It makes its own light.
It is close to the stars.
It reflects sunlight.
It is lit by the stars.
qs.why: 달은 햇빛을 반사해서 보여요.

qs.q: How long does a full cycle take?
o: About a week
About a month
About a full year
About a day
qs.why: 보름달에서 다음 보름달까지 약 한 달이 걸려요.

qs.q: What does the word "reflects" mean?
o: Makes sound
Collects heat
Gives water
Bounces light back
qs.why: reflect는 빛을 반사한다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Planning the Class Trip
items.text:
Sumi: Our teacher wants us to choose a place for the class trip.
Jack: I vote for the amusement park. The rides are exciting.
Sumi: They are fun, but tickets cost a lot, and we would wait in line for hours.
Jack: Hmm, that is true. What do you suggest?
Sumi: How about the science garden? The tickets are cheap, and there is a workshop where we can make our own robots.
Jack: Robots sound great! But is it far from school?
Sumi: Only thirty minutes by bus.
Jack: Okay, you have convinced me. Let's tell the class.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the conversation?
o: Jack and Sumi cannot decide because the bus ride takes too long.
The class will visit an amusement park to ride all of the exciting rides.
Sumi persuades Jack that the science garden is a better trip.
Sumi asks the teacher to build robots for the class during the trip.
qs.why: 수미가 과학 정원이 더 좋은 선택이라고 잭을 설득했어요.

qs.q: Why does Sumi not like the amusement park idea?
o: The teacher says that parks are boring.
It is much too far from the school.
Tickets cost a lot and the lines are long.
The rides are too scary for the class.
qs.why: 표가 비싸고 줄이 길다고 말해요.

qs.q: How does Jack feel at the end?
o: He is angry at Sumi.
He is tired of waiting.
He is afraid of robots.
He likes the new plan.
qs.why: robots sound great, you have convinced me라고 했어요.

qs.q: How far is the science garden from school?
o: Half an hour by bus
One hour by bus
Ten minutes on foot
Two hours by train
qs.why: 버스로 30분이에요.

items.title: Help with a Book Report
items.text:
Eun: Dad, can you help me with my book report? I have read the book, but I don't know how to start.
Dad: Of course. First, tell me the story in two sentences.
Eun: Well, a boy finds a map in his attic and follows it to a hidden island. There he learns to trust his younger sister.
Dad: That's a good start. Those two sentences are almost a summary already.
Eun: But I want to write about the storm and the cave and the funny parrot too.
Dad: Those are details. Put the most interesting ones in the middle, but keep the first part short.
Eun: Okay. I will begin with the two sentences.

qs.q: What does Dad advise Eun to do?
o: Write about the parrot first.
Start with a short summary.
Read the book a second time.
Copy the story from the cover.
qs.why: 두 문장 요약으로 시작하고 세부 내용은 중간에 넣으라고 조언해요.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the conversation?
o: Dad reads the book about an island and tells Eun about the parrot.
Eun is upset because her father does not like adventure stories.
Eun and her father plan a trip to find a hidden island.
Dad shows Eun how to begin a book report with a summary.
qs.why: 아빠가 독후감을 요약으로 시작하는 법을 알려 줘요.

qs.q: Which of these does Dad call a detail?
o: The funny parrot
The boy's younger sister
The map in the attic
The hidden island
qs.why: 아빠가 폭풍, 동굴, 앵무새를 세부 내용이라고 불러요.

qs.q: What does Eun probably do next?
o: She throws away the book.
She asks for a new topic.
She begins with two sentences.
She writes about the storm first.
qs.why: 마지막에 두 문장으로 시작하겠다고 했어요.

items.title: Noise in the Library
items.text:
Tom: Excuse me, could you keep your voice down? Some of us are trying to study.
Lily: Oh, I am sorry. I did not notice that I was so loud.
Tom: That's okay. It's just that I have a math test tomorrow.
Lily: Me too! I was talking because I do not understand the last chapter.
Tom: Really? I can explain it if you want. We can go to the study room at the end of the hall.
Lily: That would be wonderful. Thank you so much!
Tom: No problem. Let's go before it gets crowded.

qs.q: Which sentence summarizes the dialogue best?
o: Tom and Lily argue loudly and are sent out of the library.
Lily teaches Tom the last chapter of the math book in the hall.
Tom decides to stay in the library and ignore Lily.
A noise complaint ends with two students studying together.
qs.why: 조용히 해 달라는 말이 함께 공부하는 것으로 끝나요.

qs.q: Why was Lily speaking aloud?
o: She did not understand a chapter.
She was calling a friend on her phone.
She wanted to disturb Tom.
She was reading a story.
qs.why: 마지막 장이 이해되지 않아서 이야기하고 있었다고 해요.

qs.q: Where will they study?
o: At Lily's house after school
In the school gym next door
In a study room down the hall
At a desk near the library door
qs.why: 복도 끝 학습실로 가요.

qs.q: How does Tom's attitude change?
o: He moves from being kind to being angry.
He goes from annoyed to helpful.
He stays calm and doesn't talk.
He leaves Lily alone.
qs.why: 처음엔 조용히 해 달라고 했지만 나중에는 설명해 주겠다고 도와요.

items.title: Choosing a Gift
items.text:
Ben: Dana's birthday is on Saturday, and I still have no idea what to buy.
Anna: What does she like?
Ben: She loves painting and listening to music.
Anna: Then why not buy a set of watercolor paints? They are not too expensive.
Ben: Good idea, but she already has some paints.
Anna: Maybe a sketchbook then. Artists always need more paper.
Ben: I like that. I could write a short card inside it, too.
Anna: She will love it. Let's go to the stationery shop after school.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the conversation?
o: Ben gets help choosing a gift for a friend who likes art.
Ben and Anna are painting pictures for Dana's party on Saturday.
Anna wants to buy music for Ben's birthday after school.
Dana is going to the stationery shop to buy some paper.
qs.why: 친구의 생일 선물을 고르는 것을 도와주는 대화예요.

qs.q: Why does Ben reject the paints?
o: They cost too much.
Dana dislikes painting.
Dana already owns some.
The shop is closed.
qs.why: 다나가 이미 물감이 있다고 해요.

qs.q: What do they decide to do?
o: Buy a sketchbook and write a card
Wait until Saturday to choose a gift
Paint a picture together for her
Make a music box as her gift
qs.why: 스케치북을 사고 그 안에 카드를 쓰기로 해요.

qs.q: What will Ben and Anna do after school?
o: Visit Dana's house together
Paint in the art room
Go to a music store
Go to a stationery shop
qs.why: 방과 후 문구점에 가요.

items.title: The School Newspaper
items.text:
Mr. Lee: Thanks for coming. Our school newspaper needs new writers this term.
Hana: What kind of articles do you want?
Mr. Lee: Interviews, club news, and short reviews of books or movies.
Hana: I would like to write about the cooking club. They won a prize last month.
Mr. Lee: Wonderful. Please talk to the club members and take a few photos.
Hana: How long should the article be?
Mr. Lee: About two hundred words. Keep it short, clear, and focused on the main points.
Hana: I understand. I will send you a draft by Friday.

qs.q: Which sentence is the best summary of the conversation?
o: Hana wants to cook food for the teachers at the school.
Mr. Lee asks the cooking club to take photos on Friday.
Mr. Lee explains the job, and Hana agrees to write about a club.
The school newspaper is closing because it has too few writers.
qs.why: 리 선생님이 기사 방향을 설명하고, 하나(Hana)가 요리 동아리 기사를 쓰기로 해요.

qs.q: How long should the article be?
o: About one hundred words
About two hundred words
About five hundred words
One page with photos
qs.why: 약 200단어를 요청해요.

qs.q: Why does Hana choose the cooking club?
o: She is a member of it.
It has many photos.
Mr. Lee asked her to.
It won a prize.
qs.why: 지난달 상을 받았기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does Mr. Lee mean by "focused on the main points"?
o: Include only the key points.
Add as many facts as possible.
Use long and difficult words.
Make the article funny.
qs.why: 핵심만 담으라는 요약의 원칙과 같아요.

items.title: A Phone Call About Plans
items.text:
Mom: Hello, Jiwon. How was your day?
Jiwon: Good, Mom. I stayed after school to help my friends with our science project.
Mom: That's nice. Will you be home for dinner?
Jiwon: Probably not until seven, because we have to finish the poster.
Mom: All right, but please text me when you leave school.
Jiwon: I will. Also, can Sena stay over on Saturday?
Mom: I think so. Let me check with Dad first.
Jiwon: Thanks, Mom. I will see you tonight.

qs.q: Which is the best summary of the phone call?
o: Jiwon's mother is angry because the science project is not finished.
Jiwon tells Mom she will be late and asks about a friend's visit.
Jiwon calls Sena to ask her to stay over on Saturday night.
Mom and Dad plan to come to the school and see the poster.
qs.why: 귀가가 늦는다는 것과 친구 방문 허락을 구하는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: Why will Jiwon be home late?
o: She has a dentist visit.
She is going to Sena's house.
She missed the bus.
She has to finish a poster.
qs.why: 과학 프로젝트 포스터를 끝내야 해요.

qs.q: What does Mom ask Jiwon to do?
o: Text when she leaves school
Cook dinner for the family
Meet Dad at the station
Call Sena's mother right away
qs.why: 학교를 떠날 때 문자를 보내라고 해요.

qs.q: What will Mom do about Saturday?
o: Say no at once
Call Sena's mother
Ask Dad first
Plan a trip
qs.why: 아빠와 먼저 상의해 본다고 했어요.

items.q:
Many birds fly south before winter. They look for places where food is easy to find and the weather is warmer. Some travel thousands of kilometers each year. Many fly together in large groups, which helps them save energy. Before the trip, they eat a lot to store extra energy in their bodies, and most of them return in spring.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Birds need thousands of kilometers of space in every season of the year.
Winter is the most dangerous time of the year for all animals on Earth.
Some birds can fly farther than airplanes that carry people across the sea.
Many birds travel far to warmer places to find food in winter.
items.why: 철새가 먹이와 따뜻한 날씨를 찾아 먼 곳으로 이동한다는 내용이에요.

items.q:
Our town has opened a small free library on the corner of Pine Street. Anyone can take a book home or leave one for others. Neighbors say it has made the street friendlier.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: A free street library helps neighbors share books and feel closer.
Pine Street is the longest and busiest street in the whole town.
Neighbors must leave a book each time they take one from the box.
Small libraries should replace the big town libraries in every city.
items.why: 작은 무료 도서관이 책 공유와 이웃 관계를 좋게 한다는 것이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Cheese is made from milk. First, the milk is warmed, and a special ingredient makes it thicken. The thick part is cut, pressed, and left to age. The longer cheese ages, the stronger its taste becomes.

What is the text mainly about?
o: Why some cheeses taste stronger than milk
Where the best milk can be found
How cheese is made from milk
How to press and cut a thick cake
items.why: 우유로 치즈를 만드는 과정을 설명해요.

items.q:
Kim joined the school choir because she wanted to make friends. At first she was too shy to sing loudly. After a few weeks, she felt braver and even sang a short solo at the winter concert.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Kim won the winter concert after she took singing lessons for years.
Kim became braver and made progress by singing in the school choir.
Choir students are usually shy and cannot sing alone in front of people.
Concerts at school are held every winter, and everyone must sing a solo.
items.why: 합창단 활동으로 용기를 얻게 된 김의 변화가 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Some people believe that carrots help you see in the dark. Carrots do contain vitamin A, which is good for the eyes. However, eating many carrots cannot give you night vision.

Which sentence summarizes the text best?
o: Carrots help the eyes, but do not give night vision.
Vitamin A is found only in carrots and not in any other food.
People who eat many carrots can see clearly in dark rooms.
Carrots are the only vegetable that is good for your health.
items.why: 당근은 눈에 좋지만 야간 시력을 주지는 않는다는 것이 요지예요.

items.q:
The new bus route will begin on March 1. It connects the train station, the hospital, and the city park. Buses will come every fifteen minutes from seven in the morning until nine at night.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: The city park will close on March 1 so that the buses can park there.
Buses in the city will stop running after nine o'clock at night.
A new bus route will link three places in the city starting in March.
The train station has been moved close to the hospital and the park.
items.why: 새 버스 노선 개통 소식이에요.

items.q:
Anna wanted to save money for a new camera. She stopped buying snacks after school and began selling her old toys online. After four months, she had enough money.

What is the best summary?
o: Anna bought snacks after school and sold toys to buy a bigger bag.
Anna bought her camera by spending less and selling toys.
Cameras cost more than toys, so Anna had to work for a whole year.
Selling things online is the only way for students to earn money.
items.why: 아나가 간식을 줄이고 장난감을 팔아 카메라 살 돈을 모았어요.

items.q:
Coral reefs are home to about one quarter of all sea animals, even though they cover a tiny part of the ocean. Warmer water can make corals turn white and die. Protecting reefs means keeping the sea clean and cool.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Coral reefs cover a quarter of the ocean and are famous for turning white.
Sea animals live only in reefs, so no fish can live in the open ocean.
Divers should clean coral reefs by hand every day in the summer.
Coral reefs shelter sea animals, and warm, dirty water puts them at risk.
items.why: 산호초의 중요성과 위험 요인을 모두 담은 요약이에요.

items.q:
Mr. Choi teaches music at our school. He plays six instruments, and he always wears a bright yellow scarf. His students say that he makes difficult songs feel easy because he explains each step patiently.

Which is the main idea of the text?
o: Mr. Choi wears a yellow scarf to every class and every concert.
Music classes are the easiest subject in most schools today.
Mr. Choi is a patient teacher who makes music easy to learn.
Six instruments are too many for one teacher to teach well.
items.why: 스카프나 악기 수가 아니라 친절하게 가르친다는 점이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Plastic bags can take hundreds of years to break down. They harm sea animals that mistake them for food. Many shops now charge a small fee for bags, and more people bring their own cloth bags.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Cloth bags cost more than plastic bags, so shops no longer sell them.
Plastic bags hurt nature, so shops and shoppers are changing habits.
Sea animals eat many kinds of food that people throw away at sea.
Plastic bags break down in a few days when they are put into water.
items.why: 비닐봉지의 해로움과 사람들의 변화된 습관이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Lena was nervous about her first day at a new school. She could not find her classroom, so she asked a tall boy for help. He walked her to the door and said, "Don't worry; everyone gets lost here at first."

Which sentence summarizes the text best?
o: Lena found her classroom quickly and met a tall boy in the hall.
Everyone gets lost at a new school, so classrooms should have maps.
A tall boy was nervous because it was his first day at the school.
A kind student helped Lena when she felt lost on her first day.
items.why: 낯선 곳에서 길을 잃은 레나를 친절한 학생이 도와줬어요.

items.q:
The festival begins on Friday evening with a parade. On Saturday, there will be food stands, music, and a dance contest. On Sunday, the festival ends with fireworks over the river.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: The festival lasts three days, with a parade, food, music, and fireworks.
Fireworks over the river are the main reason people go to the festival.
The dance contest is held on Friday evening after the parade.
The festival is held only on the weekend, so Friday is a school day.
items.why: 3일 동안 열리는 축제 일정을 한 문장으로 모은 요약이에요.

items.q:
When you speak with a friend, you also communicate with your face and body. A smile shows that you are friendly. Crossed arms may mean you are angry or closed. Learning to read these signals helps you understand others better.

What is the main idea of the text?
o: Smiling is the best way to make friends with a stranger.
Body language gives extra meaning to what people say.
People who cross their arms are always angry with their friends.
Speaking is easier than reading signals on someone's face.
items.why: 표정과 몸짓이 말에 추가 의미를 준다는 것이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
A hot-air balloon rises because the air inside it is heated. Hot air is lighter than cold air, so the balloon floats upward. To go down, the pilot lets some hot air escape.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Pilots must be lighter than cold air in order to fly a balloon.
Hot-air balloons are lighter than other flying machines and fly the highest.
The pilot heats the balloon every time he wants it to land.
A hot-air balloon goes up when its air is heated and down when air escapes.
items.why: 열기구가 뜨고 내리는 원리가 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Mina keeps a diary every night. She writes about what happened, how she felt, and what she hopes to do tomorrow. She says it helps her relax before bed and remember good moments.

Which is the best summary?
o: Mina writes a diary nightly to relax and keep memories.
Mina hopes to write a book about her feelings when she is older.
Writing a diary is the best way for children to fall asleep fast.
Mina forgets the good moments in her life unless she goes to bed early.
items.why: 미나는 일기를 쓰며 마음을 편히 하고 추억을 남겨요.

items.q:
Honey never goes bad if it is kept in a sealed jar. It has very little water, so germs cannot grow in it. People have found honey in old stone tombs that was still safe to eat.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Honey is the only food that people have found inside old tombs.
Sealed jars keep any kind of food fresh for thousands of years.
Honey lasts a very long time because germs cannot grow in it.
Germs grow in honey faster than in most other foods.
items.why: 꿀은 수분이 적어 세균이 자라지 못해 오래간다는 것이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Eli's team practiced every day for the school robot contest. On the day of the contest, the robot stopped halfway through the course. The team fixed a loose wire in two minutes and finished second.

Which sentence summarizes the text best?
o: Eli's team won first place because their robot never stopped.
Robots often fail halfway through a contest because of loose wires.
Practicing every day is more important than winning a contest.
Eli's team fixed a problem quickly and still did well.
items.why: 문제를 빨리 해결해 2위를 했다는 것이 요지예요.

items.q:
Public libraries now offer more than books. Visitors can borrow tools, join coding classes, and use quiet rooms for study groups. Some libraries even have small gardens and music corners.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Today's libraries offer many services, not only books.
Libraries have stopped lending books because few people read now.
Coding classes at libraries are more popular than gardens and music.
Quiet study rooms are the main reason why libraries still exist.
items.why: 도서관이 책 이외에도 여러 서비스를 제공한다는 것이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Rice is the main food for more than half the world. It grows best in warm places with plenty of water, so farmers often plant it in flooded fields called paddies. After the harvest, the grains are dried and cleaned.

What is the best title for the text?
o: The Cleaning of Dried Grains
Warm Places Without Any Water
Rice Grown in Flooded Fields
Half the World's Farmers
items.why: 논에서 자라는 주식인 쌀에 관한 글이에요.

items.q:
Jun wanted to walk to school instead of taking the bus. The trip took twenty minutes longer, but he saw the river, met a friendly dog, and arrived feeling awake. Now he walks three days a week.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Jun takes the bus because the river path is long and boring.
Jun enjoys walking to school even though it takes longer.
A friendly dog walks Jun to school twenty minutes every morning.
Walking to school is always faster than taking a bus.
items.why: 걸어서 등교하는 즐거움이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Tomatoes need sunlight, water, and good soil. Plant them after the last frost, and give each plant a stick to climb. When the fruit turns red, pick it gently. A single plant can give you more than twenty tomatoes.

Which sentence summarizes the text best?
o: A tomato plant needs simple care to give a lot of fruit.
Tomatoes turn red only if they are picked after the last frost.
Sticks are the most important thing for growing vegetables at home.
Gardens with many plants give fewer tomatoes than a single plant.
items.why: 간단한 관리로 많은 토마토를 얻을 수 있다는 것이 요지예요.

items.q:
Sam used to be afraid of public speaking. His teacher suggested he practice in front of a mirror and then in front of his dog. By the end of the term, he could give a two-minute talk to the class without notes.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Sam's dog was nervous when Sam talked in front of the mirror.
Talks to a class are always shorter than two minutes without notes.
Sam overcame his fear of speaking by practicing step by step.
Teachers say that mirrors are the best tool for any student.
items.why: 단계적으로 연습해 말하기 두려움을 극복했어요.

items.q:
Mt. Hana is 1,950 meters high and has three trails. The easiest trail takes about two hours, while the hardest takes six. Hikers must bring water and register at the gate before they start.

What is the text mainly about?
o: The history of the oldest gate in the mountain
Useful facts for people planning a hike
The reasons why hikers like to climb fast
A story about a hiker who lost his water
items.why: 등산 계획에 필요한 기본 정보를 안내해요.

items.q:
Compost is made from leftover fruit, vegetables, and leaves. Over several months, tiny living things break these scraps into dark, rich soil. Gardeners add it to their plants as a natural food.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Gardeners should throw all their leftover food away every month.
Tiny living things can be found only in dark, rich soil.
Fruit and vegetables grow better than leaves in new soil.
Compost turns kitchen and garden scraps into rich soil.
items.why: 남은 음식과 낙엽이 퇴비가 되어 식물 영양분이 된다는 것이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
The old clock tower in the town square stopped working last year. Students at the local school raised money by holding a bake sale and a car wash. This spring, the clock finally started to tell the time again.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: The clock tower stopped because students cleaned it with water.
Bake sales are the best way for a town to fix its buildings.
Students' fundraising helped repair the town's old clock tower.
The town square is now closed because of a clock tower.
items.why: 학생들의 모금으로 시계탑이 고쳐졌어요.

items.q:
Lightning is a huge spark of electricity in the sky. It heats the air around it so quickly that the air expands and makes a loud sound, which we call thunder. We see lightning first because light travels faster than sound.

Which sentence summarizes the text best?
o: Thunder is louder than lightning because sound travels faster than light.
Lightning heats air to make thunder, and light is faster than sound.
Lightning is a huge spark that happens only on hot summer days.
People should stay inside because the air in the sky is too hot.
items.why: 번개가 천둥을 만들고 빛이 소리보다 빠르다는 내용을 담았어요.

items.q:
Bora's grandfather told her about life in the countryside fifty years ago. There was no television, so families sat together at night and told stories. Children walked an hour to school and played games with stones and sticks.

What is the main idea of the text?
o: Children long ago did not like going to school.
Television took away the games children played with stones.
Bora's grandfather lived in the city for most of his life.
Life in the past was simpler, and families were closer.
items.why: 옛날 시골의 단순한 삶과 가족의 시간이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Dan started painting when he was ten. His first pictures were messy, but he kept a sketchbook and drew a little every day. Now his paintings hang in the school hallway, and younger students ask him for tips.

Which sentence is the best summary of the text?
o: Daily practice helped Dan turn a hobby into a skill others admire.
Dan's first pictures were messy, so he stopped painting for a while.
Younger students paint better than Dan because they have sketchbooks.
The school hallway is the only place where paintings can be shown.
items.why: 매일 연습해서 실력이 늘고 다른 사람들이 인정하게 되었다는 것이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
In the rainy season, it can rain for many days in a row. Farmers welcome the rain because it fills the rice fields, but cities may flood when water cannot flow away quickly. Good drains and green parks help the water soak in.

What is the main idea of the text?
o: The rainy season lasts longer in cities than it does in the countryside.
Heavy rain brings both benefits and problems, and cities can prepare for it.
Farmers dislike rain because it fills the rice fields too quickly.
Green parks are the only way to stop all floods in a city.
items.why: 비의 좋은 점과 문제점, 그리고 도시의 대비책이 핵심이에요.

items.q:
Ming learned to cook by watching her uncle. At first she only washed vegetables, then she cut them, and finally she made a full soup alone. Her uncle said that cooking is learned a little at a time.

Which is the best summary?
o: Ming's uncle cooks soup better than anyone else in the city.
Washing vegetables is the hardest job for a new cook in a kitchen.
Ming gave up cooking because soup took too long to make.
Ming learned to cook step by step with her uncle's help.
items.why: 삼촌 곁에서 단계적으로 요리를 배웠어요.

items.q: Which step is best to do FIRST when you write a summary of a long article?
o: Find the main idea of the article.
Write down every example from the text.
Add your own opinion about the topic.
Copy the longest sentence of each paragraph.
items.why: 요약하기 전에 먼저 글의 중심 내용을 찾아야 해요.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong in a good summary?
o: Your own opinion about the topic
The ideas written in your own words
The main idea of the text
The most important supporting points
items.why: 요약에는 글쓴이가 아닌 내 의견이나 느낌을 넣지 않아요.

items.q: Which phrase is often used to introduce a short summary of the main point?
o: For example,
By the way,
A year ago,
In short,
items.why: In short는 '요약하면'이라는 뜻으로 핵심을 정리할 때 써요.

items.q: Which expression has almost the same meaning as "summarize"?
o: sum up
write down
look into
speak out
items.why: summarize = sum up (요약하다).

items.q: Which sentence best describes the length of a good summary?
o: It is exactly as long as the original text.
It is twice as long as the original text.
It is much shorter than the original text.
It is longer when the text has more examples.
items.why: 요약은 원문보다 훨씬 짧아야 해요.

items.q: A paragraph begins: "Exercise has many benefits." Then it lists better sleep, stronger muscles, and a happier mood. What is the first sentence called?
o: The supporting detail
The topic sentence
The conclusion
The title
items.why: 문단의 중심 내용을 말하는 첫 문장은 주제문(topic sentence)이에요.

items.q:
Read the three sentences. Which one is the MAIN idea?
(1) Pandas eat bamboo.
(2) They spend most of the day eating.
(3) Pandas have a simple diet and spend much of the day eating it.
o: Sentence (3)
Sentence (1)
Sentence (2)
Sentences (1) and (2) together
items.why: (3)은 (1)과 (2)를 하나로 묶은 중심 내용이에요.

items.q: A text says: "Reading helps people learn new words and understand other people better." A student wrote this summary: "Reading makes people smarter, richer, and more famous than others." What is the problem with the summary?
o: It is too short to be useful.
It repeats the title three times.
It adds ideas not in the text.
It is written in the wrong language.
items.why: 글에 없는 내용을 덧붙이면 좋은 요약이 아니에요.

items.good: The writer says that bees are important for farms.
bad: The writer says that bees is important for farms.
The writer say that bees are important for farms.
The writer says that bees are importantly for farms.

cz.st: The writer says that bees ___ important for farms.

items.rule: that절의 주어 bees가 복수이므로 동사는 are를 써요. 요약할 때 자주 쓰는 'The writer says that ...' 구조예요.
items.hint: that절의 주어가 단수인지 복수인지 확인해 보세요.

items.good: The passage explains how rainbows are formed.
items.ko: 그 글은 무지개가 어떻게 만들어지는지 설명해요.
bad: The passage explains how rainbows form by.
The passage explains how rainbows are form.
The passage explains how are rainbows formed.

cz.st: The passage explains how rainbows ___ formed.

items.rule: '만들어지다'는 수동태 be + 과거분사(are formed)로 나타내요. 간접의문문에서는 how 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 순서를 써요.

items.good: The article is about a girl who learned to swim.
items.ko: 그 기사는 수영을 배운 한 소녀에 관한 것이에요.
bad: The article is about a girl who learn to swim.
The article is about a girl which learned to swim.
The article is about a girl who learned swim.

cz.st: The article is about a girl ___ learned to swim.

items.rule: 사람을 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사는 who예요. learn은 'learn to + 동사원형' 형태로 써요.

items.good: Reading the text twice helps you find the main idea.
items.ko: 글을 두 번 읽으면 중심 내용을 찾는 데 도움이 돼요.
bad: Reading the text twice help you find the main idea.
Read the text twice helps you find the main idea.
Reading the text twice helps you finding the main idea.

cz.st: ___ the text twice helps you find the main idea.

items.rule: 동명사(Reading ...)가 주어일 때는 단수 취급하여 helps를 써요. help + 목적어 + 동사원형 구조도 확인해요.
items.hint: 문장의 주어 자리에 동사의 -ing 형태가 올 수 있어요.

items.good: To write a good summary, you should keep only the key points.
items.ko: 좋은 요약문을 쓰려면 핵심만 남겨야 해요.
bad: To writing a good summary, you should keep only the key points.
To write a good summary, you should to keep only the key points.
To write a good summary, you should keeping only the key points.

cz.st: To write a good summary, you should ___ only the key points.

items.rule: 조동사 should 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요. 문장 앞의 'To + 동사원형'은 목적(~하기 위해)을 나타내요.
items.hint: should 뒤에는 어떤 동사 형태가 올까요?

items.good: If you leave out the details, your summary will be shorter.
items.ko: 세부 내용을 빼면 요약문이 더 짧아질 거예요.
bad: If you will leave out the details, your summary will be shorter.
If you leave out the details, your summary is shorter will.
If you leaves out the details, your summary will be shorter.

cz.st: If you leave out the details, your summary ___ be shorter.

items.rule: 조건의 if절에서는 미래의 일도 현재 시제(leave)로 쓰고, 주절에는 will을 써요.
items.hint: if절은 현재형이므로 주절에는 미래를 나타내는 말이 필요해요.

items.good: This summary is shorter than that one.
bad: This summary is more short than that one.
This summary is shorter that that one.
This summary is the shorter than that one.

cz.st: This summary is ___ than that one.

items.rule: 짧은 형용사의 비교급은 -er을 붙이고 뒤에 than을 써요. 최상급 shortest는 than과 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: She asked me what the passage was mainly about.
items.ko: 그녀는 나에게 그 글이 주로 무엇에 관한 것인지 물었어요.
bad: She asked me what was the passage mainly about.
She asked me what the passage mainly was about it.
She asked me what does the passage mainly about.

cz.st: She asked me what the passage ___ mainly about.

items.rule: 간접의문문에서는 의문사 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 순서를 쓰고, 전달 동사가 과거(asked)이면 시제를 과거(was)로 맞춰요.

items.good: The text not only gives facts but also gives advice.
items.ko: 그 글은 사실뿐 아니라 조언도 줘요.
bad: The text not only gives facts but also giving advice.
The text not only gives facts but also gives advices.
The text not only give facts but also gives advice.

cz.st: The text not only gives facts ___ also gives advice.

items.rule: 'not only A but also B'는 'A뿐만 아니라 B도'라는 뜻이에요. 두 부분의 형태를 같게 써요.

items.good: A summary is a short version of a longer text.
items.ko: 요약문은 더 긴 글의 짧은 버전이에요.
bad: A summary is short version of a longer text.
A summary is a short version of a longest text.
A summary are a short version of a longer text.

cz.st: A summary is a short version of a ___ text.

items.rule: '더 긴 글'은 비교급 longer로 나타내요. 단수 주어 a summary에는 is를 써요.

items.good: The story has been read by many students.
bad: The story has been read by many student.
The story has read by many students.
The story have been read by many students.

cz.st: The story has ___ read by many students.

items.rule: 현재완료 수동태는 has/have been + 과거분사로 써요. 이야기(story)는 단수이므로 has를 써요.
items.hint: 이야기가 '읽힌' 쪽이에요. 수동태와 현재완료를 함께 생각해 보세요.
